articles.title: Namfrel eyes filing petition vs postponement of 2026 barangay, SK elections
articles.summary: The National Citizens' Movement for Free Elections said it is planning to file a petition for certiorari before the Supreme Court challenging the postponement of the Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan…

blocks.text: September 27, 2026 | 11:46am
Women cast their vote at Pasong Tamo Elementary School in Quezon City during the automated mock barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) elections on August 8, 2023.
STAR / Michael Varcas

MANILA, Philippines — The National Citizens' Movement for Free Elections (NAMFREL) said it is planning to file a petition for certiorari before the Supreme Court challenging the postponement of the Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE).

In an interview with DZBB on Sunday, September 27, NAMFREL Secretary General Eric Alvia said that the law is unconstitutional, arguing that it directly infringes upon the public's constitutional right to vote and choose their leaders.
“Alam namin na yung batas na 'to eh medyo unconstitutional,” Alvia said.
(We know that this law is somewhat unconstitutional.)

“itong halalan na 'to ay pang siyam na beses na 'to ah pinostpone simula nung 1994. Paulit-ulit na lang itong halalan na 'to na ginagalaw at kinakait sa atin 'no 'yung karapatan natin na bumoto na siyang nakalagda sa ating konstitusyon,” he added.
(This election has been postponed nine times now since 1994. Time and again, this election is being altered, depriving us of our right to vote as enshrined in our Constitution.)

Alvia cited the landmark June 2023 Supreme Court ruling in Macalintal vs. COMELEC, which explicitly states that the BSKE should not be easily moved unless there are compelling reasons, such as a public health pandemic or natural disasters.

“Kung yung mga ganitong rason na binibigay nila na ‘makakatipid daw’ o kaya ‘dahil may election fatigue’ o kaya kailangan daw ‘patuparin yung mga proyekto na hindi pa tapos,’ hindi ito masyadong sapat na rason ayon sa Supreme Court,” he said.

(If these reasons they are giving—such as 'saving money,' 'election fatigue,' or the need to 'finish pending projects'—are all they have, these are not sufficient grounds according to the Supreme Court.)
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed the most recent BSKE postponement law on Friday, September 25, moving the barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan elections from November 2026 to Nov. 13, 2028.
It also extended the term of incumbent officials from four to five years.
The Commission on Elections immediately canceled all 2026 BSKE preparations, including the filing of certificates of candidacy that had been set for September 28.

articles.title: US Embassy condemns Chinese interference of PH RoRe mission to Ayungin Shoal
articles.summary: The United States rallied behind the Philippines and condemned China for interfering with the Philippine rotation and resupply (RoRe) mission to Ayungin Shoal earlier this week.

blocks.text: Published September 27, 2026 11:44am
The United States rallied behind the Philippines and condemned China for interfering with the Philippine rotation and resupply (RoRe) mission to Ayungin Shoal earlier this week.
In a statement on Sunday, US Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton described the maneuvers by the China Coast Guard and the People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) as “dangerous” and “irresponsible.”

“The United States strongly condemns the use of dangerous blocking and other irresponsible maneuvers by the China Coast Guard and the People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) that threatened a collision with a Philippine vessel and prevented a lawful and routine resupply mission to Second Thomas Shoal on September 24,” Lipton said.

“We stand by our Philippine Allies and laud their professionalism and restraint. We call on the China Coast Guard and PLAN to cease the use of escalatory tactics that threaten the freedom of navigation and a free and open Indo-Pacific,” he added.

On Thursday, the National Task Force for the West Philippine Sea (NTF-WPS) reported that the task force said China Coast Guard (CCG) and People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) hindered the delivery of essential supplies to the Filipino crew aboard BRP Sierra Madre.
Meanwhile, the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) said three PLAN warships and five CCG vessels, including two (2) Houbei-class missile boats, interfered with the mission.

“While still approximately 60 nautical miles from Ayungin Shoal, M/V Lapu-Lapu and three (3) Philippine Navy and Philippine Coast Guard support vessels were hindered by the PLAN and CCG vessels,” the AFP said.
According to the Philippine Coast Guard, the planned rotation and resupply (RoRe) mission to Ayungin Shoal was discontinued at 11:08 p.m. for the safety of its personnel.

The West Philippine Sea refers to the maritime areas on the western side of the Philippine archipelago, including the Luzon Sea and the waters around, within, and adjacent to the Kalayaan Island Group and Bajo de Masinloc.
In 2016, the Permanent Court of Arbitration in the Hague ruled in favor of the Philippines over China's claims in the South China Sea, saying that it had "no legal basis."
Beijing has refused to recognize the decision. —Mariel Celine Serquiña/RF, GMA News

articles.title: China conducts naval, air exercise around Scarborough Shoal
articles.summary: China's military conducted a joint naval and air training exercise around the disputed Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea, it said on Sunday.

blocks.text: Published September 27, 2026 11:37am
SHANGHAI - China's military conducted a joint naval and air training exercise around the disputed Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea, it said on Sunday.
The training was held in the waters and airspace around the Scarborough Shoal, which ​China calls Huangyan Dao. It is also claimed by the Philippines, where ​it is known as Bajo de Masinloc.

The People's Liberation Army Southern Theater Command, in a statement on WeChat, described the operation as ⁠a necessary response to actions by "certain countries" it said had undermined regional ​peace and stability.
The Chinese military said the training "aims to test and enhance combat capabilities in safeguarding China’s territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests".
The Philippine Embassy in Beijing ​did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the Chinese ​military training around the shoal.

Scarborough Shoal, a triangular coral reef formation which surrounds a lagoon, is famed for its rich waters and marine resources. It is located 124 nautical miles off Masinloc, Zambales, and is considered within the Philippines’ 200-nautical mile exclusive economic zone, based on the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).
In 2016, the Hague-based Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) deemed Scarborough Shoal a high-tide feature, meaning a number of its rocks remained exposed at high tide.

Despite this, the tribunal found that the high-tide features at the shoal “are rocks that cannot sustain human habitation or economic life of their own” and therefore shall have no exclusive economic zone or continental shelf.
China, which does not recognize the ruling, also claims sovereignty over the Scarborough Shoal, which it calls “Huangyan Dao” and treats it as part of the Zhongsha Islands.

The PCA also said Scarborough Shoal has been a traditional fishing ground for fishermen of many nationalities and that China has unlawfully prevented Filipino fishermen from engaging in traditional fishing thereat. —Reuters/KG, GMA News

articles.title: Powerful storm batters northeast US, hundreds of flights canceled
articles.summary: Hundreds of flights were canceled and thousands were delayed as a nor'easter brought flooding, power cuts and travel disruption to cities like New York, Boston and Philadelphia.

image.caption: Authorities warned of flooding in coastal areas as high tide coincides with the stormImage: Vincent Alban/REUTERS

blocks.text: Heavy rain and strong winds pounded the northeastern United States on Saturday, forcing authorities to cancel hundreds of flights and leaving thousands without electricity.
New York, Boston and Philadelphia were in the firing line of the 'Nor'easter,' named after the northeasterly winds.
What is a nor'easter storm?
Nor'easters are large cyclones in the western North Atlantic Ocean, which typically form off the east coast of the US.
They can occur throughout the year but are more frequent between fall and early spring.
Nor'easters are almost always accompanied by heavy rainfall or snow, as well as strong winds.
What have authorities said about the nor'easter?
Residents in low-lying and coastal areas were warned of potential flooding and road closures, as the storm coincides with high tide.
"This storm is expected to bring major coastal flooding to the Mid-Atlantic Coast over multiple high tide cycles through the weekend," the National Weather Service said in its latest forecast.
"Prepare immediately for significant inundation in low-lying areas near the shore, including roads underwater and impacts to homes and businesses," it said.

Some 95,000 people in the states of New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, Massachusetts, Rhode Island and Pennsylvania were facing a power outage as of 3 p.m. on Saturday (1900 GMT), as per poweroutage.com.
Local leaders urge caution
New York Governor Kathy Kochul said the storm was particularly impacting the coastal areas of New York City and Long Island.
"Conditions are extremely dangerous. Anyone who goes in or near the water this weekend is literally gambling with their life," she said in a press briefing.
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani warned residents of the strong winds, saying "Don't travel if you don't have to."
Flights, events canceled
Hundreds of flights were cancelled due to the storm, with 253 at Boston's Logan airport alone, according to tracker FlightAware.

blocks.caption: The unusually powerful autumn storm intensified, forcing the cancelation of hundreds of flightsImage: Matthew Hatcher/AFP

blocks.text: Airlines including JetBlue, United and American have issued travel alerts, allowing passengers to change their flights without a fee.
As of 6:13 p.m. local time (2213 GMT), FlightAware said 439 flights involving US airports had been canceled and 2,459 flights were delayed.
Major cultural events have also been called off.
The Global Citizen and All Things Go Festivals in New York, and the Oceans Calling Festival in Maryland were canceled.

"Safety has to come first. This is the first time in 14 years we've had to cancel," said organizers of the Global Citizen event in Central Park, which was meant to feature Lenny Kravitz, Lauryn Hill, Alicia Keys and country stars Lainey Wilson and Shaboozey.
British Pop star Ed Sheeran's Weekend concerts near Boston were also canceled due to the storm.
About five inches (13 centimeters) of rain was forecast in areas of Massachusetts, including Boston. That's equivalent to more than a month's worth of rain.

blocks.caption: 'Nor'easter' are named so for its northeasterly windsImage: Joseph Prezioso/AFP

articles.title: PH pushes for enhanced climate finance access amid floods, other risks
articles.summary: The Philippines has called for better access to climate finance to help national and local institutions strengthen protection for communities facing floods, water insecurity, coastal erosion, and…

blocks.text: Published September 27, 2026 11:11am

The Philippines has called for better access to climate finance to help national and local institutions strengthen protection for communities facing floods, water insecurity, coastal erosion, and other climate-related risks.

Climate Change Commission (CCC) Vice Chairperson Robert Borje said climate finance should be assessed not just by the amount pledged but also by how effectively countries can access and use it to protect people, livelihoods, and ecosystems.

“Finance must follow risk and need, not only the prospect of financial return,” Borje said during the 2026 Forum of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change Standing Committee on Finance (UNFCCC SCF) in Sydney, Australia.

According to CCC, developing countries are estimated to require $310 billion to $365 billion annually for adaptation by 2035. International public adaptation finance reaching them, however, stood at only $26 billion in 2023.
Meanwhile, water and wastewater accounted for approximately 49% of tracked adaptation finance in 2021 and 2022, the largest sectoral share.
“But a large share of an inadequate pool remains inadequate,” Borje said.

The CCC official identified three priorities: clearer and more consistent accounting of climate finance; financial instruments and terms suited to the investments required; and enhanced access for national and subnational institutions.
He also called for simpler requirements and sustained support for institutions seeking climate finance.

“In many developing countries, including the Philippines, national and subnational institutions face accreditation, project-preparation and approval requirements that exceed their technical and financial capacity,” Borje added.

During the forum, the Philippines also pushed for financing that matches different climate needs, as public and concessional funds will remain important, while private and blended financing can help increase available resources.

The SCF supports the UN climate process by reviewing the climate finance system, improving coordination among institutions, and providing guidance and recommendations to the Conference of the Parties and the Paris Agreement.

Meanwhile, the CCC is the Philippine government’s lead policy-making body on climate change. Under RA No. 9729, it coordinates, monitors, and evaluates government programs and actions on climate change.

The CCC also helps set Philippine priorities, identify challenges faced by national and local institutions, and push for improvements in international climate finance policies and procedures. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: [Tambay] Eggie Apostol, Recah Trinidad: Pagpupugay sa mga alamat ng peryodismo
articles.summary: Tulad na nasabi sa mga Greek epic, pumanaw na ang dalawang alamat ng Philippine journalism, pero magpakailanman babanggitin ang kanilang pangalan

blocks.text: Noong nakaraang linggo sinakluban ng pagluluksâ ng mga Filipinong peryodista sa magkasunod na pagpanaw ng dalawang haligi ng industriya. Pahintulutan po ninyo ang abang tambay na ito na saluduhan sila — si Eugenia “Eggie” Apostol at Recah Trinidad.

May urban legend noong early ’80s sa mga estudyanteng manginginom ng UST AB tulad ng tambay na ito. Sa Piso-piso kami nagpapalipas ng oras kapag may break sa pagitan ng mga klase. Kaniya-kaniyang dukot sa allowance para ambag sa pambilí ng pangpawi ng uhaw. Malamig na San Miguel Beer ang paboritong serbesa. Pero ang mga babae kong kaklase Red Horse ang tinutungga. Mas malakas pa sila uminom kaysa sa aming mga lalaki.

Doon sa Piso-piso sa kalye Asturias halos katapat ng UST Dapitan gate ko unang nadinig ang pangalang Recah Trinidad. Yung henerasyon daw nila kasi ng mga taga-UST AB noong ’70s ang nagbansag sa Piso-piso. Mga literati ang pagkakakilanlan sa grupo nila Recah.

Yari lang ng kahoy ang estrukturang puwesto ng Piso-piso, tulad ng mga tipikal na aksesorya o bahay-paupahan sa Maynila nung panahong ito. Lumalangitngit ang nilalakarang sahig. Kahoy na walang tapete ang mesa. Kahoy din ang mga upuan. Malapad at bukas na bukas ang kupas na bintanang capiz para makapasok ang preskong hangin Maynila.

Mga dormitoryo, karinderya, sari-sari store at shop ng sastre’t modista ang makikita paglabas ng Dapitan gate. Walang pa yung mga mamahaling coffee shop at burger joints. Noong panahon iyon, dalawang restoran ang de-aircon ang malapit sa Dapitan gate, yung Janet’s at Food Pan. Parehong hindi ako nakakain sa dalawang iyan dahil hindi afford ng allowance ko.

Dahil tinapos na ni Marcos Sr. ang Martial Law noong dulo ng 1980 pinayagang mag-organisa muli ang mga student council. Ipinagbawal kasi noong Batas Militar ang mga student council, tulad ng pagsupil sa malayang pamamahayag. Pero ang totoo, sa papel lang nawala ang Batas Militar — pakitang-tao ng rehimeng Marcos dahil iyan ang kasama sa mga kondisyon para paunlakan ni Pope John Paul II ang imbitasyon na dumalaw sa Pinas.

Namulat ako sa pakikibaka noong panahon iyon dahil sa pagbabasa ng mosquito press, kasama na dito yung Mr. & Ms. magazine. Dahil yung mga malalaking mainstream media (TV, radyo, telebisyon) ay pag-aari ng mga crony ni Marcos, panay puri sa diktador ang mababasa, mapapakinggan, mapapanood dito. Ang nag-uulat o nagbibigay ng opinyon sa mga kabuktutan ng diktadurya ay yung mga maliliit na media na binansagang mosquito press. Doon sa Mr. & Ms. ko binabasa ang mga kolum nila Rene Saguisag, SP Lopez, Max Soliven. Yung nanay ko, palibhasa single parent ng tatlong growing boys, ginugupit ang pahina ng magasin para sa mga suggested ulam for the week.
Ang editor at may-ari ng Mr. & Ms. ay si Eugenia D. Apostol.

Kung tutuusin, mapanganib ang sumulat at magbasa ng mga anti-Marcos na artikulo noon. Maaari kang makulong. Kung susuwertihin, mawawalan ka lang ng trabaho. Kahit ganoon ang sitwasyon, tuloy pa rin ang paninindigan ni Ms Apostol sa Mr. & Ms. Si Recah naman naging unang editor ng Tempo, ang tabloid ng pro-Marcos na grupo ng pahayagang Bulletin Today. Panay din ang sundot ni Recah sa gobyerno sa mga editorial ng Tempo. Di nagtagal, sinibak sa trabaho si Recah. Sumunod sa kanya ang iba pang mga editor ng Tempo, kasama ang kanyang “sparring partner” na si Al S. Mendoza.
Nag-umpisa ako sa Philippine Daily Inquirer noong 1986, katatapos lang noon ng EDSA People Power at sinipa na ng taumbayan ang pamilya Marcos. Si Cory Aquino na ang pangulo.
Maliit na pahayagan lang ang Inquirer noon. Ang opisína nito ay nasa 13th corner Railroad Street, Port Area. Building iyon ng Star publications ng pamilya ni Betty Go-Belmonte.

Para sa isang uhúging sportswriter tulad ko, mind-blowing ang maging bahagi ng Inquirer at makasama ang mga idol mong manunulat. (Ang isa pang bigatin na naabutan ko sa Inquirer, bagaman hindi ko nakadaupang-palad ay ang National Artist na si Nick Joaquin. Ang kolum niyang “Small Beer” ay nasa page 1 ng PDI. Kaibigan ni Recah at Al si Ginoong Joaquin.)

Tatlong grupo ang nag-ambagan para mabuo ang Philippine Daily Inquirer. Pangunahing layunin nila ang mabigyan ng boses ang oposisyon para sa pinatawag ni Marcos sa snap elections. Ang building at ang printing press (na nasa loob ng gusaling iyon) ang ambag ng grupo nila Betty Go. Yung grupong civil society na nakilala naming mga reporter noon ay pinamumunuan nila Dr. Florangel Braid, Danilo Venida, at Anicia Mejia, bitbit ang financial backing at administrative know-how. Si Eggie Apostol ang nagdala ng office equipment, at editorial staff. Doon sa pioneering PDI group kasama ang Big 3 na mga kolumnísta na sila Max Soliven, Art Borjal, at Louie Beltran, na siyang naging unang editor in chief.

Maliit lang na kumpanya nag-umpisa ang PDI. Masikip na opisina, maingay, kulang sa gamit. Parang pamilya ang pagpapatakbo. Kaya’t yung mga reporter, Tita Eggie at Tita Betty ang tawag kay Mrs. Apostol at Mrs. Belmonte.
Ang pangarap sana ng mga orihinal na bumuo ng PDI ay maging isa itong kooperatibang mga peryodísta ang magpapatakbo. Yun nga lang, medyo nalihis ito. Ikanga sa Ingles: “life happened.”

Bandang July 1986 lumipat ang Inquirer sa bagong opisina, ang dating Madrid Restaurant sa EDSA, Mandaluyong (katabi ng noo’y Polymedic Hospital at ngayo’y VRP Medical Center). Noong araw na lumipat ang PDI sa Madrid ang araw din na pinaalam ni Tita Betty na aalis na siya ng Inquirer. (Sa ibang araw na yung kuwento ko tungkol diyan.) Kasama niyang umalis yung Big 3 na mga kolumnista.

Si Tita Eggie at ang grupo ng civil society ang namuno muna kaya tuloy pa din yung pangarap na maging kooperatiba. Noong 1987, sa bisperas ng sana’y unang company-sponsored Valentine’s Party na gaganapin sa bagong opisina sa Madrid, inanúnsiyó ng mga reporter na binuo nila ang PDI Employees’ Union. Kasabay nito sinabi sa management ng bagong silang na union na nais nilang bumuo ng collective bargaining agreement.

Bagaman nginingitian pa rin niya kami, tumamlay ang pakikiharap sa amin ni Tita Eggie. Noong unang CBA ng PDI, nakumpirma namin na kahit may tampo sa amin si Tita Eggie, ang puso niya ay nasa kapakanan ng mga peryodista. Halos patapos na ang negosasyon sa CBA, nung may dalawang probisyon na pinadagdag sa kasunduan sila Tita Eggie at yung grupo nila Dr. Braid. Una, ang magkaroon ng health insurance ang mga empleyado na tutustusan ng kumpanya. Ikalawa, ang magkaroon ng profit-sharing.

Noon at magpa-hanggang ngayon, bihira ang kumpanyang kusang nagbibigay ng bahagi ng kinita sa mga manggagawa. Hindi ito hiningi ng PDIEU. Management sa ilalim ni Tita Eggie at nung grupong civil society ang nagdagdag nito sa CBA.
Natural, wala kaming tutol. Kahit alam namin na noong panahon iyon, halos walang kinikita ang PDI.

Taga-sambot ako nung araw ng kolum ni Ka Recah. Dinidikta niya ito sa telepono (landline, dahil hindi pa naimbento noon ang cellphone), at agad ko naman tinitipa sa typewriter. Dito ko unang nakasalamuhà ang alamat.

Bukod sa sports kolum niyang “Bare Eye,” minsan idinidikta rin sa akin ni Ka Recah ang kanyang sinusumiteng mga artikulo. Sa aking pagbabalík-tanáw, proud ako na napagdaanan ko ito. Naiisip ko din na ang suwerte ko.

Malapitan kong namalas kung gaano kagaling na manunulat si Recah. Nasa hanay siya ng mga bukod-tanging journalist na — baga sa Ingles “among the rarefied group worthy of the title ‘auteurs’.” Minsan pinayuhan niya akong magbasa ng mga akda ng Amerikanong nobelistang si Ernest Hemingway. Ang sabi ko kay Ka Recah nakabasa nako ng ilang nobela ni Hemingway, at napansin kong magkahawig sila ng estílo.

Mapili at mabusisi siya sa mga salitang ginagamit niya. Minsan tapos na ang aming diktahan at naibaba na ang telepono. Tatawag pa ulit si Ka Recah at may papalitang salita o paragraph. Kailan ko lang nalaman na akma pala ang bansag namin sa kanya na “wordsmith.” Ginawaran pala si Recah noong 1978 ng Carlos Palanca Award for English poetry.

Gayunman, tumatak sa akin ang kababaang-loob ni Recah. Nilalarawan niya sa sarili niya na isa lamang “typist who is racing the rat.” Pinong-pino siya tumuligsa sa kanyang kolum sa mga isyu o personalidad na hindi niya sinasang-ayunan. Ika nga, punyal ang kanyang pangtarak sa kanyang kolum, hindi siya gumagamit ng maso.

Dahil sa kanyang kakaibang pangalan (kasi nga Recah, na tila babaeng Rico), madalas ay makatanggap siya tuwing Valentine’s Day ng mga bouquet ng rosas at kahon ng tsokolate. Nagpapasalamat siya sa nagbigay, sabay sabi na may ireregalo na siya sa “resident China doll” nila — ang kanyang maybahay na si Fe Lacsamana.

Sumilip ang pagiging literati ni Ka Recah nung binyagang niyang “Point Laureate” ang PBA player na si Ronnie Magsanoc. Malapit din niyang kaibigan ang kilalang pintor na si Danny Dalena ng Pakil, Laguna. Madalas dumalaw si Dalena kanila Ka Recah at Al Mendoza sa opisina ng Inquirer. Unang tingin mo pa lang kay Dalena, alam mo agad na artist siya dahil sa trademark niyang suot na sombrero at kahoy na bakya.
Isa pang malapit na kaibigan ni Recah ay si Ramon Tulfo. Magkasama na sila nung araw sa Bulletin Today at maging sa Inquirer.

Taong 2024, huli kong nakita si Ka Recah. Lamay iyon ng panganay niyang si Chino na nasawi sa atake sa puso. Napasakit sa isang magulang ang mamatayan ng anak. Niyakap ako ni boss, at bumulong sa tenga ko ng may makirot na tinig: “Hindi ko na naabutang buhay, Tochi.”

Nung nagretiro ako sa Inquirer matapos ang mahigit tatlong dekadang paninilbihan, sinulat ko sa isang social media post na ang highlight sa mahabang listahan ko ng good memories ay ang makapaglakad sa lilim ng mga anino ng mga higante ng Philippine journalism. Si Recah at Tita Eggie ang mga nangunguna sa listahan kong iyon.

Dahil sa kanilang mga ambag sa pagsulong ng malayang pamamahayag, nababagay kay Tita Eggie at Recah ang nasabi ng bida sa pelikulang halaw sa Greek epic ni Homer — “sasambitin ang kanilang pangalan habang panahon.” – Rappler.com
Si Chito de la Vega ay Tambay ng Rappler dalawang beses kada buwan. Kasama rin siya sa mga anchor-host ng programang Balita Kwento Serbisyo ng DZME 1530.

articles.title: Jeepney fares up to P14 starting Sept. 28; buses, taxis, TNVS also hike rates
articles.summary: Commuters will pay higher fares for public utility jeepneys starting Monday, September 28, with fare increases also taking effect for buses, airport taxis, transport network vehicle services and…

blocks.text: September 27, 2026 | 10:55am
Jeepney drivers wait for passengers along LRT-Taft Avenue and Gil Puyat stations in Pasay City during rush hour on June 25, 2025.
The Philippine STAR / Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — Commuters will pay higher fares for public utility jeepneys starting Monday, September 28, with fare increases also taking effect for buses, airport taxis, transport network vehicle services and point-to-point buses.
For traditional jeepneys, the fare for the first four kilometers will increase from P13 to P14, with an additional P2 for every succeeding kilometer.
For modern jeepneys, the fare for the first four kilometers will rise from P15 to P17, with an additional P2.40 for every succeeding kilometer.

The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) announced the new rates in an advisory posted Saturday after the Department of Transportation (DOTr) approved the LTFRB's recommendation to implement the fare increases.
Bus fares
For Metro Manila and city buses, the new fares are:

items: P15 for the first five kilometers for ordinary buses
P18 for the first five kilometers for airconditioned buses
P2.49 for every succeeding kilometer for ordinary buses
P2.98 for every succeeding kilometer for airconditioned buses

blocks.text: For provincial buses, the fare for the first five kilometers of ordinary buses will be P12.
For every succeeding kilometer, the rates will be:

items: P2.20 for ordinary buses
P2.45 for airconditioned buses
P2.60 for deluxe buses
P2.70 for super deluxe buses
P3.35 for luxury buses

blocks.text: Taxi, TNVS fares
Airport taxi fares will also increase to P115 for the first 500 meters.
There will be no change in the charge for every succeeding 300 meters and every two minutes.
For TNVS, the new base fares are:

items: P55 for hatchbacks
P65 for sedans
P75 for AUVs/SUVs
P165 for premium vehicles

blocks.text: The pick-up fare will be P15 per kilometer.
P2P, UV Express fares
Point-to-point buses will implement a 15% increase based on the existing fare for each route.
The LTFRB also announced provisional fare increases for UV Express vehicles and taxis.
For UV Express, the provisional increases are:

items: P2.60 per kilometer for traditional UV Express
P3 per kilometer for modern UV Express

blocks.text: For taxis, the provisional flag-down rates are:

items: P65 for regular taxis
P80 for Premium Silver Taxi Service
P95 for Premium Gold Taxi Service

blocks.text: Public transport operators are required to display the updated fare matrix inside their vehicles before collecting the new fares.
The fare increases were previously approved but their implementation had been suspended. The DOTr subsequently approved the LTFRB's recommendation to lift the suspension.
The new approved fares for jeepneys, buses, airport taxis, TNVS and point-to-point buses will take effect on September 28.

articles.title: Four killed in helicopter crash near Montreal
articles.summary: The victims of the crash have not yet been identified, Quebec provincial police told the BBC.

blocks.text: Four people have died after a helicopter crashed in a small town 50km (31 miles) from Montreal, Quebec's provincial police have told the BBC.

Emergency services were called to Sainte-Brigide-d'Iberville shortly after 14:30 local time (19:30 BST) on Saturday afternoon, where they found the aircraft on fire and declared its occupants dead at the scene.
The victims have not yet been identified but the aircraft appeared to be a private helicopter, Sergeant Audrey-Anne Bilodeau said.

An investigation into the crash is being led by the Major Crime Unit of the Sûreté du Québec, working alongside crime scene technicians as well as investigators from the Transportation Safety Board of Canada.
The crash site is located near the Rang des Écossais road off Highway 10, according to Bilodeau.
In an emergency call, police were notified of a helicopter in distress that may have crashed and caught fire.
An hour after the call, the fire at the site had been brought under control though officials were still working at the crash site just before 22:00 local time (03:00 GMT).
The victims have not yet been identified and Sergeant Audrey-Anne Bilodeau said this process may "take a few days."

articles.title: Pacquiao dares 'traitorous Filipinos' to visit Pag-asa Island
articles.summary: Newly appointed National Anti-Poverty Commission (NAPC) lead convenor Manny Pacquiao dared Filipinos, who have questionable allegiance to the country, to come and visit Pag-asa Island amid the…

blocks.text: Published September 27, 2026 10:29am

Newly appointed National Anti-Poverty Commission (NAPC) lead convenor Manny Pacquiao dared Filipinos, who have questionable allegiance to the country, to come and visit Pag-asa Island amid the tensions between China and the Philippines.
In Jonathan Andal’s report in “24 Oras Weekend” on Saturday, some residents of Pag-asa Island are already used to the Chinese vessels surrounding them.
“We are not afraid because I don’t think they will harm us given that we are civilians,” said Myra Gonzales.
But there are others who cannot help but worry about their situation.
“I wish there’s a Filipino vessel on standby. For us fishermen, we cannot help but worry,” said Fernan Lozada, a fisherman and local government employee.
For his part, Pacquiao condemned the presence of Chinese ships inside Philippine territory.
“Naiinsulto tayo, kasi in our territory, nandiyan sila. Parang nabu-bully tayo,” he said during his first visit to the island which is located 500 kilometers west of Puerto Princesa City in Palawan.
(It’s insulting that they are in our territory. It seems that they are bullying us.)
“Doon sa mga Pilipino na medyo traydor, dapat pumunta kayo dito para ma-experience niyo ba,” Pacquiao added.
(To those Filipinos who are slightly traitorous, you should visit here and experience what it’s like.)

Alongside Pacquiao, Presidential Adviser for Maritime Concerns Andres Centino, House Deputy Majority Leader Keith Flores, Aklan Representative Jesus Marquez, and other government personnel also visited Pag-asa Island to extend assistance to the municipality.
“I cannot express how happy I am. This is the first time that almost all government agencies sent representatives to visit us,” said Kalayaan Mayor Billy Alindogan.
Compared to conditions on the island a few years ago, Kalayaan has seen development. The airport now has a cemented runway along with a hangar and terminal.
The seaport was also improved. There are also newly built school buildings.
A rural health unit is also being built to serve residents.
During the recent visit of government officials, Alindogan took the opportunity to relay his requests for their town such as typhoon-resilient housing, a drainage system, and an evacuation center.
The Kalayaan Mayor also sought for a water filtration system and a new municipal hall.
“We will talk to the House Speaker regarding the requests of the mayor,” said Flores. —Vince Angelo Ferreras/RF, GMA News

articles.title: At UN, Russia and Germany’s top diplomats hold first talks since 2022
articles.summary: A source claims German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul used the talks to urge Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov to do 'everything possible to reach an agreement on grain exports via the Black…

blocks.text: UN. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov addresses the 81st United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City, US, September 26, 2026.
Eduardo Munoz/Reuters

A source claims German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul used the talks to urge Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov to do 'everything possible to reach an agreement on grain exports via the Black Sea'

items: Russian and German foreign ministers met for the first time since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, discussing bilateral ties and the ongoing war.
Tensions remain high, with Lavrov stating he learned nothing new from his German counterpart, while Wadephul urged for constructive engagement on grain exports amid food shortages.
The meeting highlighted Germany's firm stance against Russia's aggression, with calls for a cease-fire and a pragmatic solution to the conflict.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

The foreign ministers of Russia and Germany met in New York on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly on Saturday, September 26, in the first such talks since before Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

Relations between Moscow and Berlin, a close ally of Ukraine, have been frozen since the Russian invasion, and tensions escalated further after a drone incident at Leipzig/Halle Airport in eastern Germany in August.

In a sign of the continued frostiness, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov told a news conference that he had learned nothing new from his German counterpart in the talks that Berlin had not already said publicly in its official statements.
“I told him that frankly … you could just have called me and said: ‘read my statement’,” Lavrov said.
Still, the ministers discussed bilateral ties and the war in Ukraine, officials from both sides said.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul used the talks to urge Lavrov to do “everything possible to reach an agreement on grain exports via the Black Sea,” a German delegation source said. The meeting comes amid diplomatic efforts to revive Russia and Ukraine’s Black Sea grain and energy exports that have been sharply curtailed by attacks on vessels and port infrastructure.

Lavrov told the news conference that Russia had been in talks with India, Egypt and Turkey about proposals to ensure safe navigation in the Black Sea, potentially involving bilateral deals between Russia and those countries.
“There is a need for separate discussions with the Ukrainians, and not in the language of requests, but rather demands,” he said, blaming Ukraine for the attacks on vessels.
Ukraine has said it is open to agreements and blames all the fallout from the war on Russia and its invasion.

Wadephul told Lavrov, “Time is of the essence: given the food shortages in many countries — particularly in the Global South — all parties must be willing to engage constructively,” the German delegation source said.
The German minister also told Lavrov that “a pragmatic solution could pave the way for further concrete steps”, the source said.
In a sign of the sensitivities around meeting the wartime Russian foreign minister, Wadephul notified his European allies of the meeting afterwards in a message seen by Reuters.

“I used this opportunity to reiterate our position on Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine and to call for an immediate and complete cease-fire, most pressingly with a focus on grain exports, and the energy infrastructure,” he wrote.
The German government said this month it had concluded that Russia was responsible for that attempted drone attack. It closed a consulate and a Russian cultural centre in Berlin in retaliation.
The Russian embassy in Berlin has dismissed the allegations as “fabricated provocation” and as “a new wave of anti-Russian hysteria in Germany.”
Wadephul used the talks to call on Russia “to abandon the dangerous path of escalation vis-à-vis Germany, Europe, and NATO,” according to the delegation source.
Wadephul said incidents such as the attempted attack in Leipzig or further hybrid attacks would not shake Germany’s resolve to support Ukraine, according to delegation sources. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Iran says it will wait for official US response after Trump rejects Strait of Hormuz proposal
articles.summary: The US president earlier said that Tehran only made the proposal to open the strait within seven days because "they're losing so badly".

blocks.text: Iran has said it will wait for an official response from US negotiators after President Donald Trump rejected a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping within seven days.
In a post on Telegram, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi acknowledged Trump's rejection, but accused the president of previously making contradictory statements.
Earlier, Trump told reporters at the White House that Tehran's proposal was not "acceptable" and that they wanted to make a deal to open the strait immediately because "they're losing so badly".
On Friday at the UN, Araghchi told reporters that an agreement could be reached if "necessary conditions are met" between the two countries.
Araghchi said the conditions to open the strait were the same that had been included in a memorandum of understanding between the US and Iran that was signed in June.
Iran said it had raised reopening the strait and ending hostilities during negotiations on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York this past week.
The vital waterway through which around a fifth of the world's gas and oil supply usually flows has been effectively closed since the outbreak of war in February.
"I'm rejecting their deal," Trump said on Saturday, adding that the US already had "total control" of the strait, with "massive amounts of oil" passing through it.
Araghchi wrote on Telegram that Trump "has made many good statements, as well as many contradictory ones, which unfortunately we hear frequently".
"We are waiting for the mediators to convey the definitive views to us, and we will make a decision based on them," Araghchi said.
Oman, which has been acting as a mediator between the US and Iran, called for all parties to continue having open dialogue to resolve the crisis.

Oman's foreign minister, Sayyid Badr bin Hamad bin Hamood Albusaidi, told the UN General Debate that "all parties" should cooperate with Oman in efforts to safeguard navigation in the strategic waterway.
Trump's rejection of Iran's proposal was backed by the US ambassador to Nato, Matthew Whitaker.
Speaking to Fox News on Saturday, Whitaker said that Iran had offered "half measures" and "illusory deals to make themselves look good on the world stage".
"President Trump's right to reject it," he said.
Meanwhile, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Saturday that economic pressure from the US was taking a toll on Tehran.
Posting on X, Bessent said Turkey, Oman and the United Arab Emirates had halted flights from various Iranian airlines, and some banks in the UAE and Turkey had stopped transactions with Iran.
The Trump administration has dubbed an economic blockade on Iran as "Operation Economic Outcast", and is using sanctions to pressure Tehran to stop attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz.
But some economists have questioned whether the latest sanctions will be effective, as this depends on the reaction from Iran's major trading partners.
These include China, the biggest buyer of Iranian oil, which has ignored previous US sanctions and continued to do business with Tehran.

articles.title: Spain: Thousands protest in Madrid against housing crisis
articles.summary: Tens of thousands rallied in the Spanish capital after an 87-year-old woman was dramatically evicted from her home this week. Protesters called for measures to curb rising costs and reduce evictions.

image.caption: The rally was a response to the eviction of an 87-year-old woman Image: Susana Vera/REUTERS

blocks.text: Tens of thousands of people protested in central Madrid on Saturday to denounce Spain's housing crisis.
The demonstrators called for better protection for tenants, anti-fraud rules and a ban on evictions without alternative housing.
The march through the center of the Spanish capital was called after an 87-year-old woman, Maricarmen Abascal, was evicted from her apartment where she had lived for seven decades.

blocks.caption: Protesters carried signs reading 'we are all Maricarmen'Image: C. Carvajal/JNA/ZUMA/picture alliance

blocks.text: The case highlights the growing pressure on long-term tenants in Spain's major cities, where rental prices have surged in recent years. Gentrification and the shortage of affordable housing have fueled public discontent ahead of a general election next year.

Analysts say tourism and immigration-driven population growth has put pressure on the already limited housing supply in the cities. The Bank of Spain estimated a shortage of 550,000 homes across the country last year.
Toxic tourism — Mallorca's housing crisis
Protesters camp out in Puerta del Sol

Government authorities estimated that around 25,000 people had shown up to protest against Spain's growing housing crisis. The Madrid Tenants' Union, which organized the protest, said over 300,000 had taken part.

Once the rally wrapped up, some activists set up a protest camp in the city center's Puerta del Sol square with plans to stay put. Some even pitched up tents to stay the night, or until the police forcibly removed them.
Police officers looked on at about a dozen tents, surrounded by thousands of protesters, news agency AFP reported from the scene.

blocks.caption: Spain previously built homes with public funds that were later sold into private ownershipImage: Tomas Calle/JNA Press/Sipa USA/picture alliance

blocks.text: Rallying around Abascal
The protest was triggered by Maricarmen Abascal's dramatic eviction on Wednesday from the house she had lived in for decades.
Abascal was greeted by supporters as she was removed from her home on a stretcher and loaded onto an ambulance.

"We're here because housing is a problem that already affects all of society, all ages and classes," said protester Dora Garcia, a 55-year-old nurse. "And we can't keep maintaining this. Housing is a right, and we don't have it," she said.

According to Spanish media, Abascal's father first rented the home in the upscale Retiro neighborhood in 1956. After her parents died, she continued to live in the flat, which had a rent cap at the time.
Spain: Tourism boom worsens housing crisis
In 2018, the building changed ownership, and Urbagestion, an investment fund, bought the unit, raising the rent from €500 ($570) to €2,650 ($3,018).
Abascal had been offered an opportunity to buy the apartment before this but could not afford it.

The fund later lowered her rent to €1,650, but Abascal could not afford that either. Courts had blocked her eviction three times previously and extensive media coverage turned her into a symbol of the crisis.

"This whole housing situation is heartbreaking. Maricarmen has been, in a way, the last straw that sparked this social unrest, but we've been dealing with this whole issue for a long time now," said protester Simón de la Riva, 43, a teacher.
"It's unacceptable that vulture funds are buying up homes, that people can't afford to live, that entire families are being evicted, and that an elderly woman has been evicted," she added.

articles.title: ‘Queenie’ strengthens as it nears PAR exit
articles.summary: Typhoon Queenie (international name: Surigae) slightly intensified as it accelerated north-northeastward, state weather bureau PAGASA said Sunday.

blocks.text: September 27, 2026 | 9:45am
Satellite rendering shows Severe Tropical Storm Queenie (international name: Surigae) taken as of 4:40 a.m. of Sept. 27, 2026.
PAGASA via Facebook
MANILA, Philippines — Typhoon Queenie (international name: Surigae) slightly intensified as it accelerated north-northeastward, state weather bureau PAGASA said Sunday.
In its 5 a.m. bulletin, PAGASA said Queenie was carrying maximum sustained winds of 130 kilometers per hour near the center, with gusts of up to 160 kph.
It is moving north-northeastward at 15 kph.
The center of Queenie was estimated at 685 kilometers northeast of Itbayat, Batanes as of 4 a.m. Sunday.
PAGASA said strong to storm-force winds extend outward up to 300 kilometers from Queenie's center.
Sea conditions
PAGASA said moderate seas of up to 2 meters are expected over the northern seaboard of Batanes in the next 24 hours.
Mariners of motorbancas and similarly sized vessels were advised to take precautionary measures while venturing out to sea and, if possible, avoid navigation under these conditions.
Other coastal waters are expected to have wave heights of less than 2 meters.
Track, intensity
Queenie will move generally northeastward over the majority of the forecast period.
On the forecast track, the center of Queenie may exit the Philippine area of responsibility between noon and afternoon Sunday.
Outside the PAR, it will accelerate northeastward toward the sea south of mainland Japan.
PAGASA said Queenie will intensify further while moving over the sea south of the Okinawa Islands.
After reaching peak intensity, Queenie is expected to weaken by Monday, September 28.

articles.title: LTFRB says transport operators who will hold strikes will face sanctions
articles.summary: The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board warned transport operators that their franchises could be compromised if most of their fleets won"t operate amid planned transport strikes.

blocks.text: Published September 27, 2026 9:37am

The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) warned transport operators on Sunday that their franchises could be compromised if most of their fleets won’t operate amid planned transport strikes.
LTFRB acting chairman Greg Pua Jr. said that operators may be issued with a show-cause order and fined with P5,000 for first offense if they failed to operate as provided in their franchises.

“Actually, nakalagay ‘yan sa kanilang prangkisa na huwag matigil 'yung pagbibigay serbisyo nila. Shino-show cause natin ‘yan at ang minimum po diyan ay P5,000 sa first offense,” he told Super Radyo dzBB.
(Actually, it is stipulated in their franchise that their service must not be interrupted. We issue them a show-cause order, and the minimum fine for that is P5,000 for the first offense.)
He further warned that second and third offenses may warrant suspension and cancellation of franchises, respectively.

“Mayroon tayong rules on abandonment na kung ikaw ay hindi tumakbo, kung ikaw ay fleet, kung ikaw ay less than 60% ang tumatakbo for a certain period of time, your franchise will be deemed abandoned at kakaselahin ng gobyerno,” he said.

(We have rules on abandonment—if you fail to operate, and if you are a fleet operator where less than 60% of your units are running for a certain period of time, your franchise will be deemed abandoned and canceled by the government.)
Manibela is set to hold a transport strike from September 28 to 30, while PISTON will stage protests from September 29 to 30.

The strikes coincide with the first day of the fare increase for public utility vehicles. Under the new rates approved by the LTFRB, the minimum fare for ordinary jeepneys will increase from P13 to P14 for the first four kilometers. The fare for every succeeding kilometer will rise to P2.
For modern public utility jeepneys, the minimum fare will increase to P17, with an additional P2.40 for every succeeding kilometer.
Bus fares are also expected to go up. Meanwhile, taxis and UV Express services will also implement provisional fare increases starting Monday.
The fare increase is in response to the rising fuel prices that have been hurting drivers and operators.
The LTFRB said that it is in constant talks with transport groups regarding their concerns.
“Very open naman po tayo diyan… Lagi naman nakitang pinapakinggan 'yung kanilang hinaing na kung ano pa ang maitutulong ng gobyerno sa hanay ng transportasyon,” said Pua.
(We are very open to dialogue on that matter... We consistently listen to their concerns to see what further assistance the government can extend to the transport sector.)
However, estimates showed that fuel prices may roll back on September 29 following weeks of price hikes. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: NAMFREL eyes filing petition for certiorari vs BSKE postponement
articles.summary: The National Citizens' Movement for Free Elections (NAMFREL) on Sunday said it is planning to file a petition for certiorari before the Supreme Court challenging the postponement of the Barangay and…

blocks.text: Published September 27, 2026 9:27am

The National Citizens' Movement for Free Elections (NAMFREL) on Sunday said it is planning to file a petition for certiorari before the Supreme Court challenging the postponement of the Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE).
NAMFREL Secretary General Eric Alvia disclosed the group’s plans as he called the law “unconstitutional.”

“Humihingi lang ako ng clearance sa council namin kung maghahain kami ng Petition for Certiorari sa Supreme Court, pero sigurado na may hakbang kaming gagawin para tutulan ito dahil alam namin na ang batas na ito ay unconstitutional,” Alvia told Super Radyo dzBB.

(I’m just seeking clearance from our council on whether we will file a petition for certiorari before the Supreme Court. But we are certain that we will take steps to oppose this because we know that this law is unconstitutional.)

“Kaya namin tinututulan ang batas na ito, ito ay humahadlang sa karapatan natin para bumoto at mamili ng ating mga pinuno. Itong halalan na 'to, pang-siyam na bases na itong pinostpone, simula 1994,” he added.
(We are opposing this law because it hampers our right to vote and choose our leaders. This election has already been postponed for the ninth time since 1994.)
NAMFREL has expressed dismay over the postponement of the BSKE and said that it will support and join efforts to question its constitutionality.

"A government genuinely intent on addressing the crises it cites — fiscal pressure, the need for efficient and accountable frontline service delivery — should be seeking a renewed and fresh mandate for barangay leadership, not extending the tenure of officials without a single vote cast in their favor," NAMFREL said.

"NAMFREL's position on this point has not changed: economic hardship is, if anything, all the more reason to ensure accountable, freshly-mandated leadership at the level of government closest to the people — not less," it added.
On Friday, President Ferdinand Marcos signed into law a bill postponing the BSKE to 2028 and extending the term of barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan officials from four to five years.

Marcos said the move will allow officials to use the postponement "to further improve service delivery, complete programs that have already been initiated, and focus more intently on the needs of every community, family, and the youth."
Alvia pointed out that the term extension and the postponement of the elections should be treated as separate issues.

“In the guise of postponing the elections, ang ginawa nila, itinulak nila ang pagpapahaba nila ang termino ng mga barangay at SK official,” Alvia said. “Dapat hindi arbitrary 'yung pagpili ng haba ng termino.”
(Under the guise of postponing the elections, what they did was push for the extension of the terms of barangay and SK officials. The length of the term should not be chosen arbitrarily.)
The Commission on Elections had said that it already spent P8 billion of its P19-billion budget for the BSKE.
The poll body added that some election supplies, including indelible ink, may go unused if the BSKE is postponed. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: OpenAI halts training of latest models as reports mount of AI agents going rogue
articles.summary:
Decision follows disclosures that OpenAI agents searching government websites had acted in unexpected ways

OpenAI said it has paused training of its latest artificial intelligence models as…

blocks.text: OpenAI said it has paused training of its latest artificial intelligence models as reports of AI agents going rogue mount.

The decision to halt development came just hours after the company disclosed Friday that it was reviewing several incidents from the summer in which OpenAI agents searching federal government websites acted in unexpected ways beyond what was asked of them while gathering and distributing information.
Separately, the AI evaluator Transluce said agents that appeared to come from OpenAI tried unsuccessfully to hack into a US Department of Education website, a detail that OpenAI has not confirmed.

OpenAI said in a statement that it will resume training “only when we are confident that we have additional safeguards” in place, adding that it expects it will have to “hit pause” again as AI develops and other issues emerge.

AI labs are facing pressure from lawmakers and tech experts to slow development so they can build guardrails to stop agents from acting on their own, hacking websites and disclosing nonpublic information. The heads of both OpenAI and rival Anthropic have called for a slowdown too.

It is the second time in three months that OpenAI has halted development of its models. The first came in July after disclosure of a cyber-attack targeting AI startup Hugging Face, a now notorious incident that raised fears the industry was losing control.

In a meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping this week, Donald Trump agreed to share information on AI dangers and coordinate efforts to keep it safe. Trump believes AI fears are overblown, though, and later suggested that he plans no crackdown of his own.

The US is not going to be “putting on brakes”, Trump told reporters outside the White House. “They want to stop our progress because we’re leading China by a lot, and we’re going to keep it that way.”
The latest OpenAI incidents did not appear to involve the disclosure of any nonpublic information but were concerning enough for the company to warn the federal agencies involved.
In the education department incident, OpenAI agents found API “developer keys” to access government data, though ultimately only publicly available information was gathered.

In another case involving the securities and exchange commission, agents found information freely available to all but then posted it elsewhere on the internet, an act that went beyond what they were instructed to do.
US Securities and Exchange Commission spokesperson Kurt Hopfenspirger said on Saturday that “no nonpublic information was accessed”.
The Department of Education said earlier that it found “no evidence of any impact to our website or databases”.
Several other AI companies have disclosed incidents of their models going rogue and even hacking websites.
OpenAI’s CEO, Sam Altman, said in a social media post on Friday that the Hugging Face incident “is still the most severe event we’ve seen”.
OpenAI previously shared six other reports of “unexpected or concerning” behaviour in AI models and introduced a framework for tracking, probing and disclosing instances.

articles.title: ‘Cash grab’: One Nation demands up to $630,000 from Victorian election candidates
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Many applicants left feeling ‘used, lied to, misled and gaslit’, complaint letter seen by Guardian Australia says

  • Listen to the Guardian podcast

blocks.text: One Nation could collect as much as $633,000 from people who have put their hand up to run in the Victorian state election, with potential candidates questioning whether the party is staging a “cash grab”.

Guardian Australia has spoken to multiple former councillors, mayors and deputy mayors who expressed an interest in running for the party. They claim they went through what one called a “pay-to-play” application process, after which they were rejected.
Those who applied to be considered were required to pay $150 as a “non refundable application fee”, invoices seen by the Guardian show.

One Nation told the Guardian that 1,209 people put in an expression of interest to run in the November state election, and approximately 220 proceeded to the final stage, resulting in an estimated $33,000 flowing into party coffers if all final stage candidates paid this amount.
Applicants were also expected to be party members, with this translating to an additional $72,000 based on the minimum membership fee of $60 a year.

In addition, candidates were advised in interviews that they would be required to pay $5,500 of their own money to run if preselected, even though the vast majority of lower house electorates are not deemed winnable.
While it is not uncommon for the major parties to require candidates to pay an application fee, they do not levy campaign fees on candidates like those being charged by One Nation.

The candidate fee will bring $528,000 into the party’s coffers, based on running 88 lower house candidates and eight for the upper house. In total, the amount paid by candidates could be as much as $633,000.
Aidan McLindon, a political consultant who worked with One Nation in Victoria last year, said many potential candidates had been left frustrated by what appeared to be a “money-spinning exercise”.
One Nation was “disproportionately focusing on profits over policy”. McLindon said in an interview for episode three of The Populist, out on Monday.
Based on the party’s polling numbers, One Nation is also in line to receive as much as $10m through Victoria’s public electoral funding scheme.

Applicants who spoke to the Guardian have questioned whether the application process was genuine, saying the party had conducted 15-minute video interviews with each candidate before a decision was made. Potential candidates were all required to sign non-disclosure agreements about the process on application.

There is also concern that the upper house candidates were “captain’s picks” selected by the party’s state leader, Warren Pickering, with One Nation overlooking candidates with significant local government and professional experience.
A complaint letter sent to the party by one former Victorian mayor says the process has left many candidates feeling “that we were used, lied to, misled and gaslit”.

“The issue is that the process increasingly looks as though it was used as cover to conceal decisions that had already been substantially made, while creating the public appearance of an open, merit-based candidate search,” the letter seen by the Guardian states.

“Applicants should not have been encouraged to invest their time, energy, reputations and personal information in an elaborate exercise merely to provide legitimacy, numbers or political cover for what now appears to have been a biased and self-serving leadership process.”
after newsletter promotion
Another local government member who had applied questioned whether the process was a “cash grab”.
“They are asking everyday folk, hard-working mums and dads, for $5,500 which is a lot of money,” one said.
“I just think it is a cash grab for the federal election. My feeling is they are just using all of the states to fundraise for the federal election where they want to take power.”
Another said they believed that under the party’s constitution, all funds would be transferred to One Nation’s Brisbane headquarters.
“They will get $800,000 in the kitty for doing absolutely nothing,” one said.
A spokesperson for One Nation said the party uses “a nominal cost recovery model to do police and other checks on candidate nominees”.
“All candidate fees have been paid into the Victorian state campaign account in accordance with the Victorian Electoral Commission rules.
“Application fees and campaign contributions are a standard requirement implemented by all major parties within Australia.”
The Guardian has previously reported that candidates at the 2025 federal election were left out of pocket by the party’s candidate funding agreements.

articles.title: Christa Pike to be first woman executed in Tennessee in 200 years - but her defence say she's a victim too
articles.summary: Lawyers for Pike, who killed a fellow student in 1995, say she should get clemency and would not be sentenced to death if the crime happened today.

blocks.text: Christa Pike to be first woman executed in Tennessee in 200 years - but her defence say she's a victim too

blocks.caption: Image caption, Christa Pike's lawyers have filed a clemency petition seeking to commute her sentence ahead of the 30 September execution date

blocks.text: Image source, Tennesse Department of Corrections
Christa Pike's lawyers have filed a clemency petition seeking to commute her sentence ahead of the 30 September execution date
ByStephanie Hegarty
BBC World Service Correspondent

Ashlee Sellars last heard from her friend Christa Pike earlier this week, when Pike texted her from her cell on death row as she prepares to be killed by lethal injection by the US state of Tennessee.
Pike told Sellars she does not want any of her loved ones to be present on Wednesday when she is executed.
"She doesn't want us to experience that," Sellars says.
Sellars finds it hard to reconcile this woman, whom she has only known to be kind and protective, with the person who committed a heinous crime 31 years ago.
Pike, now 50, was 18 when she and her boyfriend at the time, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and murdered Colleen Slemmer, a 19-year-old they met at a job training camp for troubled teens.
The murder created a media frenzy in Knoxville, Tennessee in 1995 when Colleen was found with a pentagram, a symbol of Satanic ritual, carved into her chest.

Pike had accused Colleen of insulting her and trying to steal her boyfriend. Two other residents at the camp later testified that Pike had bragged about the murder before and after, and showed them a piece of Colleen's skull.
A year later she was sentenced to death, while Shipp - who was 17 at the time - was given a life sentence with the possibility of parole.

Now, after years of failed appeals, Pike's execution has been set for Wednesday. If it goes ahead, she will be the first woman put to death in Tennessee in more than 200 years. Only 18 women have been executed in the US since the 1970s, compared to 1,663 men.
Colleen's mother has said she wants Pike's execution to happen so that her daughter "finally can be resting".

blocks.caption: Image caption, Student Colleen Slemmer was tortured and brutally killed in the 1995 murder

blocks.text: Image source, Family handout
Student Colleen Slemmer was tortured and brutally killed in the 1995 murder
But Pike's lawyers, who filed a 226-page clemency petition, are still hoping for a last-minute reprieve, and UN human rights experts have also called for the execution to be stopped., external

Pike has a documented history of childhood sexual abuse, abandonment and neglect. Her lawyers believe that if she was found guilty of the same crime today as a teenager she would not receive a death sentence.
In the years since her sentencing, her defence team have uncovered details about her childhood that they say the jury never had the chance to consider.

"It is mind-boggling that they did not present any of her history of abuse and rape, even though they knew about it," says Sandra Babcock, an expert in gender and the death penalty at Cornell Law School, who has worked on Pike's defence.
"Her case is so uniquely compelling, not just because of her really incomprehensible history of sexual violence but the combination of that with her youth and her mental illness."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Christa Pike suffered neglect and was abused by her parents

blocks.text: Image source, Christa Pike
Christa Pike suffered neglect and was abused by her parents

In 1995, forensic psychologist Dr Diana McCoy was hired by Pike's defence team and found she was severely neglected by both of her parents. McCoy's report found Pike was physically and sexually abused by several of her mother's husbands and boyfriends, and raped several times, once when she was 11 and again aged 17. Later it was discovered that she was repeatedly raped as a toddler by her grandmother's boyfriend. McCoy said Pike's mother didn't believe her that these rapes happened.

But Pike's trial lawyer did not put McCoy on the stand or call many of the witnesses she recommended. These details emerged more than a decade later in a court hearing reviewing her case, when a new team of lawyers claimed ineffective assistance of counsel, a claim that was denied by the judge.
In 2021 Pike was diagnosed with bipolar disorder in prison and has been medicated since.

Later, another forensic psychologist working for Pike's defence, Dr Bethany Brand, who assessed Pike in 2023, said her case was extremely rare because she was abused by so many people who should have protected her.
"Her childhood was replete with physical, sexual, and emotional abuse. She was sexually violated by a number of men, starting before she was school age," she says.

Brand says Pike had untreated manic episodes due to bipolar disorder and untreated PTSD. "Both of those things together absolutely influenced how threatened she felt by the girl she ended up killing and her lack of emotional control in that situation."

Babcock adds: "If they let her be executed, then what it tells us is that the death penalty in this country is just a joke. It's not for the worst of the worst. It is for the people who receive the worst legal representation and who are the most damaged and vulnerable."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Pike, pictured as a teenager, killed Slemmer in January 1995 after telling a friend she "just felt mean that day", court documents say

blocks.text: Pike, pictured as a teenager, killed Slemmer in January 1995 after telling a friend she "just felt mean that day", court documents say
'She should pay for it'
Last year, Tennessee's Supreme Court ruled Pike had not shown circumstances that would justify commuting her sentence. Her appeals process had been exhausted and a date was set for her execution.

A federal appeals court had earlier ruled that the jury had already heard about her difficult childhood during testimony from her mother, father, and aunt during her trial. And that new evidence of bipolar disorder, PTSD, and brain damage "mostly repeated" what the jury had heard and would not have changed the verdict.
The row has some parallels with the high-profile case of murderer Lisa Montgomery, whose lawyers also argued she was a mentally ill victim of abuse who deserved mercy.
Montgomery's legal challenges failed to commute her sentence, and she was executed by lethal injection in Indiana in 2021.

Unless she is granted clemency by Tennessee Governor Bill Lee, Pike will be executed on 30 September. That decision is unlikely to come until the last moment, and Lee has never granted clemency in a death penalty case before.
The Tennessee Supreme Court this week denied Pike's request to halt the execution. Her counsel say they have been discussing next steps.

On her execution day, Pike has requested an all-female team. She says being held down by a group of men will exacerbate her trauma. The state of Tennessee has said the goal is that female guards will transfer Pike to the prison where she will be executed but hasn't guaranteed it.
Colleen's mother May Martinez supports Christa's execution.
"She did the crime. I think she should pay for it," she said on Knoxville TV station WBIR in 2021, and told the BBC this week she still stands by those comments.
Pike should suffer before she dies, Martinez told WBIR. "I would feel better that she felt the same pain that Colleen did."

blocks.caption: Image caption, May Martinez, mother of Colleen Slemmer, and a retired Knoxville Police department detective outside a courtroom for a post-conviction hearing in 2006

blocks.text: Image source, J. Miles Carey/USA TODAY/Imagn Images via Reuters
May Martinez, mother of Colleen Slemmer, and a retired Knoxville Police department detective outside a courtroom for a post-conviction hearing in 2006
"My heart breaks every single day because I keep reliving it and reliving it, and I can't no more, and I want this to happen before I die," she added.
"There's not a day goes by that I don't think about Colleen or how she died and how rough it was. I just want Christa down so I can end it, relieve my daughter, so she finally can be resting."
The Justice Coalition, a victims' rights advocacy group, has raised money to help Martinez travel to Tennessee to watch the execution.
The group's executive director, Robert Bracewell, said this sentence was determined by a jury of Pike's peers and it is what Colleen's family want.
"We stand firm with the family that on the 30 September her execution ought to proceed."

Ashlee Sellars grapples with two seemingly conflicting beliefs: that Colleen's mother has a right to feel justice has been served and that everyone, including her friend Christa, deserves a chance at redemption.

"When I think about reconciling who you see on TV or the horrible tragedy that happened with Colleen, the only thing that makes sense to me is around mental health and trauma and the way that people process stuff in a moment when they don't have the things that they need," Sellars says.
"These horrible things happen in your youth and then those traumas moved through you, in our community, and you cause harm to somebody else."

Sellars met Pike in prison while serving a 25-year sentence for her involvement in a robbery-murder. They spoke to each other through the meal flaps in their doors on the high security unit. Now, Sellars works as an advocate for justice reform and victims of crime.
"People want to know that everyone's life matters, right? They want to know that Colleen's life mattered," she says.
"Christa in this moment, I think she is fighting much more for her life to matter than she is to actually live."

blocks.text: Albanese says announcement of Medicare breach ‘purely in national interest’

Anthony Albanese says he was not aware of other cases of AI agents wrongfully accessing classified information before he revealed OpenAI’s unauthorised infiltration of the Medicare Statistics Reporting portal in New York on Thursday, Australian Associated Press reports.
“At the time we made our announcement … we weren’t aware of other occurrences,” the prime minister told reporters at Sydney airport on Saturday.
“We were acting purely in our national interest.”
The PM landed back in Australia on Saturday after a week in the US where he addressed the United Nations General Assembly on the international need to rein in AI.
He said news that autonomous agents allegedly infiltrated American university and commerce department sites, as well as the US Securities and Exchange Commission, further proved that need.
“We now know it wasn’t just the issue of the Australian sites that have been subject to AI agents accessing information without authorisation,” Albanese said.

double quotation markWhat this does is confirm that approach of making sure that it needs to be an appropriate national response, as well as an international response to make sure that humans are in charge of this new and emerging technology.
Albanese said it was up to OpenAI to state why multiple breaches occurred.
Good morning

Welcome to our Sunday live blog. Flight delays and cancellations caused frustration and heartache for some footy fans racing to make it to Saturday’s AFL grand final before the first bounce. And the PM says the timing of his announcement of OpenAI’s Medicare hack was made “purely in the national interest”. More on both those stories shortly.
Also, the Liberal deputy leader, Jane Hume, will be speaking on the ABC’s Insiders this morning. More on that coming up.

articles.title: In UN address, Anand takes jab at 'great powers' disrupting global order
articles.summary: Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand has put "strategic autonomy" at the forefront of Canada's address to the United Nations General Assembly today.

blocks.text: World·New
Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand has put "strategic autonomy" at the forefront of Canada's address to the United Nations General Assembly today.
Speech echoes Carney's recent rhetoric for strong middle power alliance
State sovereignty 'has been treated with disdain,' Anand says in UN address
Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand says Canada's foreign policy is guided by establishing autonomy in strategic fields to limit superpower coercion, along with aspirations to lead middle powers.
"Great powers are walking away from global economic co-operation, dismantling economic integration," Anand said Saturday in Canada's annual address to the United Nations General Assembly.
"In the face of this rupture, Canada's goal is to achieve greater strategic autonomy," she said at the green marble dais.

Anand's speech echoed Prime Minister Mark Carney's rhetoric over the past year about middle powers forging deeper ties and working with countries on shared goals, including states that aren't close partners.
She said that involves emerging technologies, critical minerals, defence production and energy — as well as the rule of law and respect for sovereignty.
"We are facing serious challenges in the global order," Anand said.

"We will lead other middle powers to act collectively and decisively, because middle powers are playing a key role in building the framework for the new international order — which is being established as we speak."
Anand used an analogy that she said comes from her roots in rural Nova Scotia. "The tide does not wait; you must move with it."
Anand said state sovereignty "has been treated with disdain" but that Canada will defend that principle, and work toward stability and common rules.
She said that is why Canada is calling for a just peace in Ukraine, self-determination for Palestinians and Israelis, and an end to hate-based violence.
"We were tragically reminded of the scourge of antisemitism again when a gunman carried out an attack on a synagogue in Belleville, Ont.," she told the UN.

"Canada is an open, pluralistic society, with a public square full of robust and civil debate. Our success is underpinned by this civility, by our democratic institutions and by respect for our differences," she said.
For the second year in a row, Anand spoke instead of Carney, who was at the UN from Monday to Wednesday but whose officials said he could not deliver Canada's address due to scheduling issues.

The UN schedules foreign ministers later in the rotation during the annual high-level week, with weekday, daytime speeches reserved for heads of state and government. Anand spoke late Saturday afternoon.

Anand also voiced support for the NATO alliance, amid an increase in warnings from European leaders about Russian hybrid attacks. She cited a recent defence agreement between Denmark, its autonomous territory Greenland and U.S. President Donald Trump.
"This agreement is yet another reminder that North America and Europe are stronger together. And as a founding member of NATO, our commitment to the transatlantic alliance is ironclad," Anand said.
To that end, Anand reiterated work being done to better secure the Canadian Arctic, saying this is occurring in lockstep with Indigenous Peoples.

Anand said Canada supports the International Criminal Court amid Washington's quest to dismantle the institution. Her comments come as Canadian critics argue Ottawa is not calling out American coercion, including the sanctioning of a Canadian judge for her work at the ICC.
She reiterated Canada's bid for a seat on the UN Human Rights Council, through a vote expected in one year.
Anand said Ottawa is pursuing "values-based realism" while advocating for democracy in Iran, the return of Ukrainian children kidnapped by Russia and work to end Haiti's gruesome gang crisis.
Her speech mentioned gender equality, LGBTQ+ rights, Sudan's civil war, Hamas attacks on Israel, Israeli settler violence against Palestinians and safe approaches to artificial intelligence.
Anand also said Canada is ready to work with whoever UN members elect as their next secretary general, referring in French to the role in the masculine and feminine titles.
That comment followed the Trudeau government calling for a woman to be the next secretary general, in September 2024. The Carney government has not repeated that call.
